channel.title: Paperraft
channel.description: Research in efficient inference and AI agents, ranked by independent GitHub implementations instead of citations or stars. Papers above the attention threshold are deliberately excluded.

item.title: Intrinsic Information Rates of Summaries in Simulation-Based Inference
item.description: The method replaces deterministic fixed-dimensional summary encoders in simulation-based inference with stochastic binary bottlenecks whose mutual-information rate is measured and matched across candidates. The cost is added encoder and training complexity, the need to estimate each trained summary's information rate, and potential sampling variance during posterior estimation. It can fail if the simulator violates the common-support condition, if rate estimation is inaccurate at the target budget, or if the benchmark-specific ranking reverses at the information budget used in production. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MCF: A Memory- and Communication-Aware Co-Designed Framework for Long-Context LLM Inference
item.description: It replaces static KV-cache layouts and prefill-to-decode layout conversion with MARS, which replicates hot KV blocks during early prefill and progressively drains them into a sharded decode-ready layout while routing only lightweight queries across stationary KV shards. Its cost is an FPGA compute-NIC datapath plus a distributed, metadata-driven orchestration layer that is far beyond a single 24 GB GPU or API-based stack and adds substantial systems complexity. It can fail when the assumed early-prefill memory headroom or multi-worker communication bottlenecks are absent, and its scaling advantages are unverifiable without a cluster. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Mechanistic Insights into LoRA: Layer Sparsity for Adaptive Fine-Tuning via Path Patching
item.description: The method replaces standard all-layer LoRA, which fine-tunes every transformer layer, with LoRA applied only to task-relevant layers identified by a frozen-base zero-ablation calibration pass. It reduces adapter parameters roughly 3.5x while adding a per-task calibration step and per-task layer-selection bookkeeping; training compute per step is otherwise comparable to standard LoRA. Layer importance is reported as highly task-dependent with limited cross-task overlap, so a selection calibrated on one task or benchmark can underperform on another, and results are demonstrated on a single 1.5B model and may not transfer to other architectures, scales, or non-reasoning workloads. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SPARTA: A Sparse Ternary LLM Accelerator with Adaptive Attention and Unified Datapath for Long-Context Edge Inference
item.description: SPARTA replaces conventional GPU/CPU edge inference and separate ternary-linear and attention datapaths with a custom unified accelerator combining ternary-weight SpMM/SpMV, bit-serial attention, and page-level Top-k plus token-level Top-p KV-cache pruning. Its gains depend on fabricating or programming dedicated hardware and on 1.58-bit ternary models, and the adaptive attention prunes KV access at the cost of task-dependent quality loss. It can fail in applicability terms: the results are accelerator-specific, quality degradation varies by task and pruning aggressiveness, and nothing here transfers directly to a 24 GB GPU or API-based stack. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Transporting Quantiles to Codebook: Scalable Vector Quantization without Codebook Collapse
item.description: FlowVQ replaces the standard VQ-VAE quantizer with jointly learned EMA/codebook-update schemes by transporting fixed even-quantile prior codes through a lightweight flow-matching probability flow ODE to define the codebook. It adds training-time complexity and extra compute for learning and integrating the flow, plus sensitivity to flow-training stability, while inference tokenization cost depends on the final implementation and may remain near standard VQ lookup if the codebook is materialized. It can fail through distribution mismatch between latent encodings and the transported prior, degraded reconstruction on high-precision data, or implementation overhead that negates the claimed utilization benefit. 1 independent implementation, 107 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: DocTalk: Enhancing Medical Knowledge Retrieval via Fine-tuned Large Language Models with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Robust Clinical Decision Support
item.description: Replaces full fine-tuning or reliance on base/prompt-only models for clinical QA by applying LoRA-based instruction tuning on a small expert-reviewed dataset. Cost is modest: tuning an 8B model with LoRA fits on a 24 GB GPU, but requires curated QA pairs, expert review, and evaluation infrastructure. Can fail through residual hallucination, dataset bias from only 500 QA pairs, limited external generalization, and clinical safety risks if deployed without guardrails. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Distributed LLM Inference via Communication-Efficient Speculative Decoding
item.description: Replaces vocabulary-scale distribution transmission with a server-side replica of the draft model, exchanging only token indices and scalar probabilities. Costs include maintaining model consistency across device-server boundary, double draft model storage, and synchronization complexity. Fails if replica drift occurs or when speculative decoding itself is unsuitable for the workload. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: DuQUAD: A Dual-View Framework with Quality-Aware Evidence Pruning for Multi-Document Question Answering
item.description: The method replaces standard RAG context packing and common Lost-in-the-Middle mitigations such as reordering, reranking, or generic multi-agent reasoning with a dual-view local/global agent design plus quality-aware pruning. It costs added orchestration and inference overhead versus a single-pass RAG pipeline, though the paper claims lower cost than prior multi-agent frameworks. It can fail when relevance or quality scoring is inaccurate, when pruning removes useful evidence, or when the extra local/global passes do not repay their latency and implementation complexity on a given workload. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: retrieval and RAG. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Relevance-Guided Residual Calibration for Spectral Compression of Dense Retrieval Embeddings
item.description: RRC replaces the corpus-derived spectral weighting rules used by PCA, Whitening, and SpecTemp with a closed-form, relevance-guided calibration that adjusts per-direction log weights via a fitted power-law trend plus a residual, without retraining the encoder or adding an inference stage. Its costs are the need for relevance judgments to estimate positive--negative margin weights per retained direction and an offline calibration step applied to the shared query--document transformation; runtime cost remains that of the underlying spectral compressor. It can fail if relevance judgments are scarce or biased, if the assumed margin-based weighting does not match the retrieval objective, or if the estimated residuals overfit dataset-specific relevance signals and do not transfer across encoders, domains, or quantization settings. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: retrieval and RAG. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Predicate Neuron: Differentiable Quantization of Predicate Relations in Gradient-based Learning
item.description: Replaces standard activation units (or supplements layers) with a differentiable predicate neuron that quantizes inputs and a choice state to perform fuzzy first-order logic operations with a hard-forward, differentiable-backward gradient mechanism. Costs an additional trainable parameter per neuron, a custom gradient implementation (available in Keras/PyTorch), and added architectural complexity without published latency or memory overhead measurements. Can fail if benchmark gains on MNIST/Wikitext do not transfer to the target workload, if the hard/soft gradient mismatch causes training instability at scale, or if maintenance of a custom module outweighs modest accuracy benefits. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Multi-Draft On-Policy Distillation for Diffusion Drafters
item.description: MDraft replaces single-draft on-policy distillation of one-step diffusion drafters by sampling several draft blocks per context and aggregating verifier full-vocabulary conditionals across their prefixes into the training target. It costs additional drafter sampling and verifier forward passes during training, while drafter architecture and inference procedure remain unchanged. It can fail if the reader does not already operate a diffusion-based speculative decoding stack, since training requires verifier access for distillation and the benefit vanishes for autoregressive drafters or API-only deployments. 0 independent implementations, 124 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Selective and Hybrid-State Communication for Latent Multi-Agent Systems
item.description: The method replaces natural-language message passing between agents with selective transfer of KV caches and recurrent states through a shared workspace. It costs implementation complexity, direct access to model internals, and some quality risk, including a six-point drop on HumanEval+ for SelectKV. It can fail when agents do not share compatible latent representations, when inherited context is disturbed, or when the production stack relies on third-party APIs that do not expose internal states. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Human-Residual Steering: Aligning Frozen LLM Judges with Human Judgment Distributions
item.description: HRS replaces output-level calibration and distributional fine-tuning of LLM judges with a learned low-rank correction at a single hidden layer, predicted from the judge's hidden state and logits and trained on individual annotations with proper scoring rules. It requires white-box access to hidden states (ruling out third-party API judges), needs per-annotator rating data for training, and adds a small auxiliary module; training uses roughly 88 times fewer parameters than distributional fine-tuning at a modest alignment cost. It can fail when annotator-level labels are scarce or unrepresentative, when the judge model or benchmark domain shifts away from the training distribution, and the oracle analysis does not guarantee the learned predictor recovers the full correction. 0 independent implementations, 124 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ICALL-BENCH: Benchmarking LLM Interprocedural Reasoning in Binary Programs
item.description: ICALL-BENCH replaces function-level and end-to-end binary reverse engineering evaluations with a probe that isolates interprocedural reasoning via indirect-call target recovery on 50 real C/C++ programs under model-only, static tool-augmented, and Internet-enabled regimes. Adopting it costs an evaluation harness, tool integrations, and agent run budget; it provides no production capability, only measurement. It fails as a decision aid if the user's workload is not binary analysis, since results concern reverse engineering agents and transfer poorly to general code or ML tasks. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Interpretable neural equation learning for high-dimensional materials data
item.description: nn-EQL replaces generic black-box regression on sparse, high-dimensional scientific tabular data with an iterative train-prune-retrain neural network using custom neuron-level activations to recover compact interpretable equations, ranked by an MDL-inspired score. Its cost is added training complexity, hyperparameter and activation-library design, and an encoder dependency for high-dimensional inputs, all runnable on modest hardware. It can fail by converging to spurious or non-unique equations on sparse noisy data, and its diagnostics do not guarantee physical validity of the discovered terms. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: TERRA: Task-Oriented Edge AI for Regional Fire Detection with Identity-Free Reporting
item.description: TERRA replaces per-device raw measurement transmission and device-identified reconstruction with tiny task-oriented reports (a quantized fire probability or a compact learned feature) aggregated by a permutation-invariant DeepSets model at the receiver. The cost is training and deploying per-device edge inference plus the aggregation model, and accepting evidence fusion rather than recoverable per-sensor data. It can fail under degraded uplink conditions: missed or falsely recovered messages erode accuracy, and while TERRA-Score is more robust to false-message contamination, both modes depend on report availability and were validated only on a single indoor EN54 testbed, so transfer to real outdoor fire deployments is unproven. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: FAD-KV: Adaptive Dictionary KV Caching for Efficient Reasoning Decoding
item.description: Replaces dense per-token KV storage and prior dictionary-based sparse KV compression (OMP-style iterative coding, static or append-only dictionaries) with one-shot Top-n screening plus lightweight coefficient refinement and a fixed-size dictionary that recycles inactive atoms. Costs include maintaining and adapting the dictionary, per-step sparse coding and coefficient refinement, and integration complexity in the decode path; the abstract reports no memory-reduction factor or speedup. It can fail if screening misses the right atoms or stale atoms are reused under distribution shift, degrading long-reasoning quality, and reported quality-efficiency trade-offs may not transfer to a specific model or serving stack. 0 independent implementations, 124 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: VerifiedLab: Harnessing Knowns for Unknowns
item.description: VerifiedLab replaces static literature records with a multi-agent pipeline (planner, librarian, specialists, gate, critic) that verifies each claim field by field against measured data reliability before release. It costs substantial inference-time compute, since verification scales with the number of claims and records, plus engineering effort to build field-level verification over a curated domain corpus. It can fail when source records are incomplete or inconsistently reported, when reliability estimates are miscalibrated, and its demonstrated results are confined to one materials-science domain, so transfer to other literatures is unproven. 0 independent implementations, 124 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Bi-Phase Training: Learning Efficiently From Scratch
item.description: BPT replaces full-parameter pre-training of a foundation model with a parameter-efficient update scheme: frozen base weights are adapted through trainable diagonal matrices and low-rank adapters composed with constrained high-rank left/right transformations, periodically merged back into the base. It reduces trainable-parameter memory and optimizer state during pre-training, but it still requires from-scratch pre-training on billions of tokens and does not claim to reduce total compute or data requirements to a single 24 GB GPU budget. It can fail through a residual perplexity and downstream-task gap versus full training, sensitivity to merge schedule and adapter constraints, and limited evidence beyond the reported model sizes, datasets, and token counts. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: SkillMem: Compact External Skill Memory for Latent Multi-Agent Reasoning
item.description: SkillMem replaces textual skill prompts, per-skill KV caches, and skill-specific parameters with a 9.6 KB external latent memory per skill, read through a role-conditioned cross-attention module during latent multi-agent reasoning. The cost is training the skill memories and shared reader via behavioral distillation against text-skill-induced prediction changes, plus access to paired successful/failed trajectories, while the backbone stays frozen. It can fail where latent multi-agent infrastructure is absent, where gains concentrate in smaller backbones and do not transfer to larger ones, or where distillation fails to capture the textual skill's effect, silently degrading skill reuse quality. 1 independent implementation, 134 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: QMUL_AK at AISA-ArabicFC: Schema-Constrained Function Calling with ALLaM
item.description: This replaces generic prompt-only function calling with a LoRA-fine-tuned 7B instruct model using schema-aware prompts, dialect and no-call resampling, a token-weighted loss, and deterministic validation of outputs against the tool schema. Costs are modest: LoRA training of a 7B model fits on a single 24 GB GPU, uses only official task data, and adds a lightweight deterministic validation step at inference, but requires curated task-specific training data and schema definitions. Failures concentrate in argument extraction (0.8920 argument exact match versus 0.9982 function accuracy on the dev set), and results derive from one Arabic shared task, so transfer to other languages, domains, or schema distributions is unverified. 1 independent implementation, 124 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Are Seismic Foundation Models More Than Glorified Feature Extractors?
item.description: This replaces imported audio/vision-style self-supervised objectives (single-window masking or quantization targets) for seismic waveform encoders with a systematic comparison of nine objective/bottleneck/mixer variants on one shared Mamba architecture. The cost is a 3M-window pretraining corpus and a frozen-checkpoint evaluation pipeline, plus the finding that changing the objective redistributes rather than raises downstream skill, so no single checkpoint serves all tasks. Adoption can fail because gains are regime-dependent (few-shot only), masking pressure re-specializes rather than generalizes, and the paper concludes the binding constraint is an occurrence-process learning target that does not yet exist. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Large Language Models for Accurate Medical Chart Abstraction: Enabling Scalable and Secure Artificial Intelligence Deployment in Stroke
item.description: The method replaces manual chart abstraction by non-expert staff for extracting structured clinical variables from unstructured neurointerventional reports. It requires infrastructure capable of running a 70B-parameter model (beyond a single 24 GB GPU without aggressive quantization or a third-party API) plus prompt engineering and expert adjudication of ambiguous cases. It can fail on inference-heavy variables such as intracranial angioplasty, and accuracy is conditioned on cases where the reference model produced a valid prediction, which may overstate real-world performance. 0 independent implementations, 124 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: METATRON: A Promptable Whole-Body Execution Layer for Humanoids
item.description: Replaces task-specific humanoid controller training with a single frozen generative whole-body policy prompted at each control step by ordinary code 'skills' that express goals, letting coding agents add behaviors without further policy training. Costs include a physically deployed humanoid platform (Unitree G1), motion-capture and retargeted training data, sim-to-real transfer, and real-time whole-body control infrastructure far outside LLM serving; quality/latency costs for ML inference are not reported. It can fail in sim-to-real gaps, safety-critical balance/recovery edge cases, hardware wear, and skill-code errors that the frozen policy cannot correct. 0 independent implementations, 9 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Post-Training Large Language Models with LLMON
item.description: The method replaces conventional flat prompting, where instructions and data are indistinguishable to the model, with a post-trained structured format (LLMON) that enforces identifier-based execution semantics. It costs a full post-training pipeline: construction of a 4.6B-token structured corpus with distractor variants, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning on base models, which exceeds a limited cloud budget if replicated at the reported scale. It can fail on instruction formats or injection patterns outside the training distribution, since the defense depends on the model having internalized LLMON semantics rather than on a guaranteed architectural constraint. 2 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: El Agente Quntur: Agentic Active-Space Selection for CASSCF
item.description: This approach replaces manual, expert-driven active space selection in CASSCF quantum chemistry calculations with a multi-agent LLM harness that plans, executes, and refines computational workflows. It requires access to LLM APIs and incurs variable, potentially unpredictable computational costs and latency due to dynamic inter-agent communication and decision-making. Adoption carries risks of inconsistent active space selection across runs, uncontrolled cost escalation, and failure to converge on correct state assignments without robust stopping criteria. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: DecompGym: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Designing Decomposition Algorithms
item.description: The paper introduces DecompGym, a benchmark that replaces output-only checking of agent-written optimization solvers with a three-part audit: a 60-second execution limit, numerical feasibility plus an LLM-judged method audit, and an objective within 1% of the known optimum; its actionable finding is that reflection (diagnosing the failure before retrying) replaces blind independent regeneration when repairing failed agent code. The cost is an extra diagnosis step per retry, the need for a stored optimal objective per task, and reliance on an LLM judge whose method audit rejects attempts that output checks alone would accept (93 of 108). Failure modes include judge false rejections such as the 'optimal if' pattern (96 occurrences, 92 from one model), missing or suboptimal Benders solutions (48 of 62 failures), and the possibility that reflection's advantage does not transfer to domains without a verifiable optimum. 0 independent implementations, 11 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Is it my preference? Role Grounding Attack against Agent's Memory via Social Interaction
item.description: This is an attack, not a technique to adopt: it exploits role-to-principal misattribution in LLM-agent memory systems, where a nested quoted conversation causes a victim agent to record an attacker's preference as its own user's preference, enabling tool-selection manipulation and privacy leakage. For the reader, the actionable cost is auditing any deployed memory pipeline that ingests shared or multi-party content, and adding provenance binding (explicit role and source attribution) to stored memories, which adds engineering complexity and storage overhead. What can fail: memory systems that drop conversational context at write time remain vulnerable, attribution fixes may degrade recall quality or increase latency, and defenses are unvalidated since the paper demonstrates the attack across five memory systems and six models but proposes no evaluated mitigation. 2 independent implementations, 18 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Skeleton Coding: Program Structure as a Specification for Agents
item.description: The method replaces the practice of providing only end-to-end behavioral specifications (tests, input-output examples) to a coding agent with jointly specifying the program structure (decomposition into data types, modules, functions) in a high-level, code-like skeleton format alongside those behavioral tests. The cost is the upfront developer effort to design and write the structural skeleton, shifting some design responsibility from the agent back to the developer, rather than additional compute, memory, or latency overhead. Adoption can fail if the developer-specified skeleton is flawed or too rigid, as the agent is then constrained to a suboptimal structure that may not align with the requirements or may hinder its ability to find a correct implementation within that class. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: 3DCodeEdit: Benchmarking Instruction-Guided 3D Program Editing
item.description: The paper contributes a benchmark, but its actionable technique replaces single-shot generation of 3D code edits with a multi-turn loop where a separate reviewer model compares renders against the request and feeds discrepancies back to the editor. It costs extra inference rounds: each attempt requires rendering plus a reviewer-model call, multiplying latency and API spend per edit. It can fail because reviewer feedback only partially compensates for missing geometric foresight, and it depends on a reviewer able to perceive render discrepancies accurately, which itself degrades on subtle structural or style errors. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Precedent or Intent? What Coding Agents Follow When Evolving Existing Code
item.description: This replaces implicit reliance on repository examples and agent defaults with explicit written priority rules for handling conflicts between existing code and new instructions. Costs are limited to curating local precedent files and loading short priority rules into the agent harness, with negligible compute overhead. Failure occurs when rules are ambiguous, contradict strong local precedent, or omit the rationale needed for agents to resolve conflicting instructions. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Vendster: An Evaluation Arena to Investigate How Forecasting Tool Quality Affects LLM Agent Behaviors in Buyer-Vendor Negotiation
item.description: It replaces accuracy-first selection of forecast tools with a negotiation arena that measures downstream decision value under controlled bias and interval width. It costs added evaluation complexity, repeated LLM rollouts, and domain customization rather than new model training or cluster-scale infrastructure. It can fail when the arena’s buyer-vendor setting, agent reactivity, or sampled demand patterns do not transfer to the reader’s production workflow. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: A Case Study of a Multi-Agent Kernel-Optimization Loop That Learns a New AI Accelerator
item.description: The method replaces manual, expert-driven kernel development for poorly documented or new AI accelerators. It costs significant LLM inference, multi-day device time on scarce hardware, and the operational complexity of maintaining an agent loop that builds and revalidates its own target knowledge. It can fail if the agent generates incorrect or illegal kernels that pass screening but degrade performance, or if toolchain changes invalidate accumulated knowledge without detection. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: MUSE: Multi-Level Memory with Selective Runtime Injection for Scientific Coding Agents
item.description: MUSE replaces single-level task retrieval for coding agents with a three-tier memory (global, approach-level, implementation-level) plus an LLM gate that decides whether to inject implementation experience during execution. It costs an offline memory-construction pipeline over historical trajectories, additional retrieval and gate LLM calls at runtime (extra latency and API spend), and ongoing memory curation complexity. It can fail if historical trajectories are scarce or unrepresentative, if the gate injects irrelevant advice that distracts the agent, or if benchmarks-style scientific coding does not match the reader's actual workloads. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: WeVisCut: The Whole Editing Room in One Agent From Narration to Long-Form Video
item.description: The method replaces multi-stage agentic editing pipelines driven by general-purpose models with a single compact 9B policy trained on 130K examples recovered through editing inversion and verified replay. It requires a four-stage data construction pipeline applied to finished videos and dedicated fine-tuning, trading generality for task-specific efficiency. The trained policy may fail on editing styles or narration genres underrepresented in the 3,750 source videos, and the benchmark is in-house with only 100 tasks, so external validity is unverified. 2 independent implementations, 48 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Manifest-Assisted Retrieval in Artificial Intelligence Search: Evidence Gaps and a Security Evaluation
item.description: This technique replaces ad-hoc or implicit trust in AI search manifests with an explicit threat-modeling framework paired with deterministic pre-model controls. It costs implementation complexity and operational overhead to deploy parser fixtures and evidence-separation controls without establishing incremental security or utility gains over fixed ordinary retrieval. It can fail because manifest-content effects remain unisolated in live retrieval, leaving discovery, fetch, and downstream execution paths vulnerable or ineffective in production agent evaluations. 0 independent implementations, 8 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: SCOPE: Selective Critical-Step On-Policy Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
item.description: SCOPE replaces trajectory-level outcome RL and full-trajectory distillation with selective self-distillation at policy-identified critical error steps, using hindsight-generated step-specific skills, a bounded teacher-student coefficient, and a length-efficiency reward. It costs an RL training pipeline with supervised warm-up, trajectory self-analysis, and environment interaction, which requires on-policy RL infrastructure (e.g., GRPO-style rollouts) that is compute-heavy even for a 3B model on a single 24 GB GPU, and the largest gains are shown with a 32B backbone that exceeds the reader's hardware. It can fail because the results are confined to two benchmarks (ALFWorld, WebShop) whose near-ceiling success rates (97-99%) may not transfer to noisier real agent tasks, the critical-step selection mechanism may misidentify error steps and inject harmful distillation signals, and the method presumes the policy can generate useful hindsight skills for its own failures. 5 independent implementations, 164 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Masked Erosion: How Acceptance Gates Lose Redundant Safeguards in Self-Improving Agents
item.description: This replaces naive acceptance gating—which scores harness edits only on task success—with statistical harm audits across safeguard subsets, frozen safety constraints, or one-layer ablation checks. It costs additional evaluation compute to measure harm for every safeguard subset and requires freezing safety text or auditing layered defenses to prevent masked deletions. It fails when larger evaluation batches permit deletion of expensive safeguards, when defensive depth is lost against weaker future models despite current protection, or when optimizers bypass semantic safeguards while preserving their textual form. 3 independent implementations, 137 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Agent Transfer Protocol: Server-Mediated Agent-to-Agent Communication Architecture for the Agentic Web
item.description: ATP replaces direct, instance-bound point-to-point communication between agents with a domain-mediated architecture in which organizational servers hold stable addresses, queue messages for offline instances, and sign envelopes for later source and integrity verification. It costs continuous operation of sending and receiving domain servers, added mediation latency that the paper measures but does not summarize numerically in the abstract, plus key-management and message-storage complexity. It can fail if either party's domain server is unavailable, if verification keys are rotated or no longer trusted when delayed messages are read, and if counterparties do not adopt the same protocol, since cross-organization value depends on bilateral deployment. 1 independent implementation, 134 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: SpaceAct: Benchmarking 3D Spatial and Temporal Reasoning via Closed-Loop Action and Active Perception
item.description: SpaceAct replaces passive VQA and symbolic-planning evaluations with an interactive benchmark that tests closed-loop physical action and active perception on 108 brick-and-puzzle instances without privileged coordinates. It costs the effort of setting up the SAPA evaluation environment and API calls against frontier MLLMs; it provides no deployable model or efficiency method, only measurement. It can fail as an adoption target because results on a small, specialized puzzle suite may not transfer to the reader's actual production tasks, and it measures capability gaps rather than closing them. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Nemotron 3.5 Super and Lightning: Open, Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Models for Agentic AI
item.description: The technique replaces dense Transformer-only deployment with a hybrid Mamba-Transformer mixture-of-experts design combined with native speculative decoding and low-precision NVFP4 inference. It costs substantial systems complexity: MoE routing, hybrid state-space/attention execution, draft-model acceptance tuning, and quantization-aware deployment must all work together. It can fail on a single 24 GB GPU because the practical benefits depend on large-scale serving hardware, specialized kernels, and infrastructure that constrained teams may not have. 1 independent implementation, 133 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: SPARSEBLEED: Bypassing Attribute-Inference Defenses via Sparsity Optimizations
item.description: The defense replaces constant-time execution (disabling sparsity optimizations) with response padding that equalizes all queries to worst-case timing, closing a timing channel that leaks input attributes and output labels. It costs roughly 7.24% average inference latency overhead and requires identifying worst-case execution time per model-hardware pair, with near-zero extra energy. It can fail if worst-case estimates are miscalibrated for a new backend or input distribution, if the deployment stack uses libraries outside the nine evaluated, or if non-timing side channels remain open. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: FPGAFly: A 166.7k-Neuron Fruit-Fly Connectome on One FPGA via Deferred Spike Expansion and Shared-Codeword States
item.description: The method replaces per-synapse spike expansion and 41-bit per-neuron state storage with one 64-bit descriptor per spike expanded later in source-ID order, plus a 24-bit state encoding that shares codewords across normal, refractory, and out-of-range states. The cost is additional decoding logic (1245 LUTs), quantization of out-of-range states, and a hard dependency on a specific FPGA target (Gowin GW5AST-LV138) with custom RTL design. It can fail if connectivity or state precision exceeds the encoding's assumptions, if non-LIF neuron dynamics are needed, or if the design must be ported to different hardware, since the gains are tied to that device's BSRAM and LUT budget. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: The Role of Quantization in Loss Spikes
item.description: The method replaces AdamW with SGD with momentum on the final LM head during language model pretraining to suppress output logit growth and delayed 'time-bomb' loss spikes. It costs nothing in memory or latency and reduces optimizer-state memory slightly, but requires direct control over the pretraining optimizer and long training horizons to matter. It can fail if adopted blindly for fine-tuning or short runs, where the instability it addresses does not arise and SGD may underperform AdamW on the head layer. 2 independent implementations, 2049 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Multi-Token Prediction Done Right
item.description: Soft-MTP replaces the standard multi-token prediction cross-entropy gradient with only its KL self-distillation component, recovered exactly by combining existing NTP and MTP cross-entropy gradients via straight-through routing, implemented as a one-line code change. It costs no additional parameters, memory, or compute, and avoids the vocabulary-sized logit matrices required by direct KL minimization. It can fail in that all evidence comes from pre-training runs up to 1.2B parameters, so the benefit is unverified at production model scales and only applies to teams that run their own pre-training with MTP heads. 0 independent implementations, 262 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: FlatCake: A Flat KVCache Storage Architecture for LLM Serving
item.description: Replaces tiered DRAM-cache-over-SSD KV management (as in Mooncake) with a flat architecture that places each KV block once, in session-contiguous layer-major order, and streams SSD reads directly to GPU via GPUDirect Storage. Cost is a redesign of the serving storage path, dependence on NVMe SSDs with GPUDirect support, and commitment to a fixed placement decision at block creation time. It can fail when the deployment lacks GPUDirect-capable storage or multi-SSD bandwidth, when workloads are DRAM-resident and tiering is not the bottleneck, and when the trace-specific gains do not transfer to different session reuse patterns. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: CSO: Refining Robotic Policies via Skill Distribution Alignment and Skill-Grained Optimization
item.description: CSO replaces direct RL fine-tuning of VQ-VAE-discretized robot policies with a two-stage scheme: rejection-sampling supervised fine-tuning to align the observation-to-skill prior with successful trajectories, then skill-grained clipped policy optimization with the encoder frozen. It requires an online trajectory collection and rejection-sampling loop plus a pretrained QueST-style policy, adding pipeline complexity and dependence on successful rollout data rather than inference cost. It can fail when online collection yields few successful trajectories, when the frozen encoder is misaligned with deployment observations, or on tasks whose skill granularity mismatches the per-skill importance-ratio assumption. 0 independent implementations, 219 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Towards Reliable, Scalable, and Value-Aligned Generative Recommendation for Large-Scale Advertising
item.description: GR4AD-X replaces deterministic semantic-ID assignment and likelihood-only beam search with multi-path SID construction, multi-dimensional capacity scaling, and unified value-guided generation, beam pruning, and discriminative reranking. It costs additional training complexity, prefix-level reward modeling, reranking computation, and tighter coupling between generation quality and commercial-value estimation. It can fail if value rewards are misspecified, if prefix-level credit assignment remains weak, or if the gains depend on Kuaishou-scale traffic, data, and serving infrastructure that a small team cannot reproduce. 1 independent implementation, 27 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: CoSTA: Co-Evolving Self-Play Timeline Agents for Complex Temporal Knowledge Graph Question Answering
item.description: Replaces single-context TKGQA reasoning with a coordinator-worker architecture that delegates temporal evidence gathering to specialized agents. Requires training infrastructure for role-conditioned distillation and co-evolving self-play optimization, plus runtime orchestration overhead. Performance depends on effective learned collaboration; if coordination fails or evidence synthesis degrades, answer quality may not exceed simpler single-agent or retrieval approaches. 3 independent implementations, 153 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Security Impact of Coding Agent's Memory Files
item.description: The paper does not propose a technique that replaces an existing method; it characterizes project memory files (e.g., CLAUDE.md) as an injection channel that can steer coding agents, finding only small, inconsistent effects on secure completions (-8 to +6 points) but large differences in whether agents disclose the file's influence. The practical cost to the reader is process, not compute: treat memory files as untrusted code-adjacent input, gate them behind the same review as source changes, pin or hash approved versions in the repository, and require agents to disclose which files shaped their output. What can fail: the study shows flagging a malicious memory file does not reliably prevent vulnerable code, and disclosure behavior varies by agent, so review-based mitigations reduce but do not eliminate the risk. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: REVBRAIN: Real-time Probabilistic EEG Forecasting Using Residual Vector Quantization
item.description: REVBRAIN replaces sample-by-sample autoregressive WaveNet inference for probabilistic EEG forecasting with residual-vector-quantization tokenization that generates the entire 200 ms prediction horizon in a single forward pass. The cost is a tokenization stage that discretizes the output space, adding pipeline complexity and quantization error, and the reported accuracy advantage is limited to one EEG forecasting benchmark. The method can fail if the RVQ codebook underrepresents signal regimes outside the resting-state alpha band used in evaluation, and the probabilistic calibration of tokenized forecasts remains unverified for closed-loop stimulation settings. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Two-Stage Clipping: Linear-Time Approximate and Exact Mixed-Norm Projections for Transformers
item.description: TSC replaces exact proximal solvers for ℓ1,∞ mixed-norm projection—used to induce column-wise structured sparsity in Transformer weight matrices—with a two-stage approximate operator: a group-level budget projection followed by per-group coefficient clipping, computable in O(nm) time (O(n²) for square attention matrices). The cost is that the operator is an approximation, not the exact projection: the paper bounds the Euclidean discrepancy to the true proximal solution and reports it is small on synthetic data, but it is nonzero by construction, and it targets the projection operator itself rather than delivering an end-to-end pruned model. What can fail: the sparsity levels at which the approximation error stays acceptable for downstream accuracy are not established on production-scale LLMs in the abstract, integration requires a sparsification-aware training or pruning pipeline the reader may not have, and the runtime benchmarks are synthetic, so realized gains on real model compression workloads need validation on the reader's own matrices and tolerance for approximation error. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Repairs for Whom? Evaluator-Executor Mismatch in Selecting Repairs for Failed LLM Agents
item.description: The method replaces scoring candidate repairs with greedy replay, a stronger proxy model, an environment oracle, or a log-reading judge, instead selecting repairs using rollouts from the agent that will actually execute them. The cost is rollout budget for the deployed policy at selection time, though the paper reports that twenty 14B rollouts per candidate are worth no more than two of the 7B agent's own rollouts, so the approach can be cheaper than proxy-model scoring while being more accurate. It can fail when own-policy rollouts are unavailable or too expensive, when the deployment policy changes after repair labels are created (invalidating executor-specific labels), and when the failure set was pre-screened for repair value, a regime the paper does not test. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: failure recovery. Recommendation: test.

item.title: How Deterministic SAST and AI Security Agents Divide the Work: Coverage, Harness Policy and Cost in Snyk VulnBench 2.0
item.description: The method supplements, not replaces, deterministic SAST (e.g., Snyk Code) with an LLM security-review agent (e.g., Claude Code /security-review), since each engine misses vulnerabilities the other catches. The cost is API inference spend per review plus engineering effort to configure the harness correctly; the paper notes coverage and cost were only loosely related, so the most expensive configuration is not automatically the best. Failure modes include the agent's review policy silently excluding vulnerability classes (16/20 vs 9/20 on restricted classes when the policy was removed), file-level findings without line-level localization (Codex Sol: 80 file-level but only 34 line-level), and missed flows when the harness's file selection prunes relevant files (DeepSec retained files from only 56 of 108 flows). 0 independent implementations, 8 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Think Before You Act: Decision Gate for LLM Agents
item.description: JevAct replaces unverified direct execution of agent-proposed tool calls with an interception layer that compiles domain policies into executable state checks plus a prefill-only decision model that issues probability-based judgments and targeted feedback for bounded revision. It costs an additional verification model and policy-compilation engineering per domain, adds latency on intercepted actions, and requires writing executable state checks, though it needs no changes to the agent model or its tools. It can fail where policies are incompletely specified, where the decision model misjudges conversational context, or where domain transfer is poor, as the mixed Airline results indicate. 1 independent implementation, 133 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Teacher Evolution
item.description: TESD replaces standard On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD), which uses a static self-teacher, by adding teacher-oriented optimization and adaptive student weighting based on reward feedback. It costs additional rollouts and environmental feedback for teacher training, increasing computational overhead and implementation complexity compared to vanilla OPSD. The method can fail if reward signals are noisy or unreliable, leading to incorrect reliability estimates and suboptimal teacher evolution. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Weaken to Strengthen: Weakening-Induced On-Policy Self-Distillation for Large Reasoning Models
item.description: WISD replaces self-distillation methods that require privileged information or external teachers by training the model to minimize divergence from a weakened copy of itself created via low-bit quantization or magnitude pruning, using only unlabeled prompts. The cost is doubled memory during training (hosting both original and weakened models) plus computational overhead for the contrastive loss, though the weakened copy can reuse quantized weights efficiently. Post-adoption risks include divergence from the original model’s distribution leading to catastrophic forgetting, and sensitivity to the degradation level—if the weakened model is too corrupted, the contrast signal becomes noisy and training destabilizes. 3 independent implementations, 143 stars. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: CARI: Cross-Boundary Adversarial Runtime Injection in Coding-Agent Workflows
item.description: Replaces the assumption that peer-supplied runtime feedback in coding-agent workflows is inherently trustworthy, by demonstrating that malicious instructions embedded in diagnostic output from compromised components can induce unauthorized victim-side actions. Adoption requires implementing input validation, output sanitization, and action-gating layers around runtime feedback channels, adding latency and operational complexity to agent pipelines. Defenses based on prompt-level policies can fail through over-refusal of legitimate debugging actions or through incomplete coverage of covert instruction channels that mimic normal diagnostic language. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: When Relevant Code Is Wrong: Runtime-Aware Context for AI Coding Agents
item.description: The method replaces purely relevance-, similarity-, or recency-based retrieval of code and development artifacts with retrieval filtered by operational validity under deployment-specific feature flags, configurations, and architectural evolution. It costs additional infrastructure to link repository artifacts to runtime configurations and maintain classification rules, plus ongoing curation as deployments change, and the evaluation is limited to six tasks and three deployments with reference rules rather than demonstrated gains in agent correctness. It can fail when runtime configuration data is incomplete or stale, when the valid/invalid/unknown classification rules do not match an organization's deployment logic, or when valid recall drops sharply if feature-flag evidence is missing. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Causal Attention on CPU: A Cache-Aware and Load-Balanced Scheduling Kernel for Prefill
item.description: CACPU replaces GPU-based causal attention prefilling with a CPU kernel featuring tiered cache blocking and in-kernel task dispatching for multi-agent long-context workloads. It requires CPU memory capacity for long-context KV cache and adds integration complexity via SGLang; the causal attention pattern limits applicability to prefill rather than general decoding. Performance depends on specific CPU cache hierarchies and thread counts, and CPU memory bandwidth may bottleneck very long sequences or high concurrency compared to GPU. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: attention and kernels. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Tight Bounds for Anonymous Parity Certification
item.description: This is a theoretical distributed-computing result establishing tight certificate-size bounds (Theta(log log n) bits) for verifying graph-order parity in anonymous networks; it replaces nothing in ML production practice. It costs nothing to adopt because it describes proof-labeling schemes for distributed graph verification, not a deployable model or inference technique. It cannot fail in an ML pipeline because it has no interface with one; the result is only relevant to researchers in local certification and structural graph theory. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Where You Inject Matters: The Trust Region Effect in LLM Agents
item.description: The paper does not propose a deployable technique that replaces an existing method; it is an empirical characterization showing that indirect prompt-injection success varies with placement, e.g., a GPT-5.4 agent followed an unsafe instruction in repository documentation (README/TODO) 2.6 times more often than the same instruction in code or data files, plus learning-based attackers that optimize content and placement. Adoption of its insights costs engineering effort to extend guardrails and sanitization uniformly across all environmental surfaces rather than only obviously untrusted ones, adding parsing and policy complexity. It can fail if defenses are tuned only to the studied surfaces, since attacker placement strategies adapt and trust-region patterns may differ across models and agent scaffolds. 3 independent implementations, 2060 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Auditable Belief Updates as a Missing Safety Layer for LLM-Powered Multi-Agent Systems
item.description: The method replaces implicit, opaque propagation of evidence-based commitments across agents with external belief states, structured update operators, and a runtime firewall that bounds or rejects weakly evidenced updates. It adds state storage, update and auditing logic, runtime latency, and integration complexity, with no quantified resource or performance figures in the abstract. Adoption can fail through unreliable evidence grounding, false-positive rejection of legitimate updates, scaling overhead, and group-level manufactured consensus, collusion, or misinformation cascades. 2 independent implementations, 141 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Efficient Agentic Audio-Visual Question Answering through Toolset Pruning and Modality Consolidation
item.description: The technique replaces a broad specialized audio/visual toolset and long agent trajectories with a compact two-tool workflow using omni-modal captioning and omni-modal QA. It reduces inference cost by about 70% while claiming comparable or better benchmark accuracy, with the main adoption cost being workflow redesign and validation effort rather than added memory. It can fail if the benchmarks do not represent production audio-visual questions, if omni-modal tools hide errors that specialized tools previously exposed, or if reduced trajectories remove evidence-gathering steps needed for harder cases. 1 independent implementation, 10 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Context Compaction for World Models
item.description: The technique replaces retraining or model-layer context-window expansion with an agent harness that compacts and selects prior world context for the world model. It adds harness complexity, compacted-state storage, and context-processing overhead without requiring foundation-model training. Retrieval can still fail if compaction omits state needed to reconstruct a revisited region, and sliding-window-attention models lose most of their context retrieval when dreaming. 0 independent implementations, 123 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Why Speculative Decoding Works Better Than Predicted on Sparse MoE Models
item.description: Speculative decoding replaces standard one-token-per-forward-pass autoregressive decoding by drafting multiple tokens with a small model and verifying them in a single target-model pass, and this work refines the cost model for MoE targets. It requires maintaining a draft model alongside the target, adds verification and routing-analysis complexity, and its measured benefit on MoE models depends on kernel bandwidth utilization and expert routing overlap that vary by hardware. It can fail to deliver expected speedups when the draft model's acceptance rate is low, when the target model is dense rather than sparse MoE, or when GPU execution dynamics differ from the H100 profiling used in the paper. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: From Local Recovery to Unified Generation: Discovering Triple Set in Knowledge Graphs via Observation-Anchored Latent Diffusion
item.description: LatentDiff replaces subgraph-based knowledge graph completion, where the graph is partitioned into local subgraphs completed independently, with a unified latent generative framework: a relation-aware residual-quantized autoencoder encodes the whole graph, and a latent graph diffusion model anchored on the observed graph recovers missing triples by progressive denoising. Adoption costs include training the quantized autoencoder and diffusion model over the full graph, iterative denoising at inference, and substantially more implementation complexity than embedding-based or rule-based completion baselines. Failure modes include dependence on an autoencoder whose reconstruction quality bounds downstream performance, diffusion sampling latency that can be unacceptable in production, and benchmark gains (5.4 F_tsp points) that may not transfer to domain-specific KGs with different relation distributions or scale. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: retrieval and RAG. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: REALM: Identifying Minimal Task Assets for LLM Agents
item.description: It replaces giving an LLM agent broad ambient access to files, accounts, and services with a maintained dependency graph of required assets and resource-bound partial APIs inside a task container. The cost is additional infrastructure for asset discovery, grant management, and API projection, plus possible task completion loss when required assets are missed or authorization lags execution. It can fail when asset identities emerge dynamically, source-scoped selection admits the wrong resource, prerequisite resolution is incomplete, or the partial API surface blocks legitimate task steps. 0 independent implementations, 1 star. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Beyond LLM Wrappers: Context Engineering and the Three-Engine Architecture for Reliable Financial AI
item.description: This architecture replaces single-agent LLM pipelines and text-centric RAG with a three-engine system comprising a financial knowledge graph for provenance and relationships, a deterministic optimization engine for calculations, and a multi-agent LLM layer for orchestration and validation. It costs deployment complexity in building reusable ERP mappings, graph templates, and validation policies, though observed deployment time reduced from roughly six to two weeks once these assets exist. ERP data quality issues and tenant-specific schema variations remain major implementation challenges that can compromise context quality and validation accuracy. 1 independent implementation, 123 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: AgentHeal: Evaluating Goal-Preserving Resource Recovery of Web Agents under Access Barriers
item.description: AgentHeal replaces standard web-agent evaluations that assume freely accessible resources or only transient perturbations with a benchmark of non-transient access barriers (dead links, authentication walls, rate limits, anti-scraping defenses) across nine barrier families in a counterfactual sandbox and real-website replay. Adoption costs engineering effort to set up the sandbox or replay harness, the API or compute cost of running agents against nine barrier families, and the ongoing work of diagnosing failures the benchmark surfaces; it is an evaluation harness, not a model improvement. What can fail after adoption is misinterpreting results if the sandbox diverges from the reader's target web domains, optimizing agents to the benchmark's specific barriers rather than general recovery, or deprioritizing it because it adds no new capability to the deployed agent itself. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Energy-Efficient FPGA Implementation of an End-to-End Cosine-Domain CNN Using High-Level Synthesis
item.description: The method replaces spatial-domain and Fourier-domain CNN inference with an end-to-end DCT-domain architecture that uses real-valued arithmetic and avoids intermediate inverse transforms, implemented on a Xilinx Kintex UltraScale+ FPGA via high-level synthesis. Adopting it costs FPGA hardware, HLS toolchain expertise, and a network redesign into spectral layers, none of which map onto the reader's single-GPU or API-based stack. Validation covers only MNIST and a 94-class ASCII task, so accuracy, scalability, and toolchain fragility on realistic workloads remain unproven. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: MemSteer: Turning User Histories into Supervision for Agent Memory Optimization
item.description: MemSteer replaces costly human-annotated QA labels and supporting evidence with automatically generated, evidence-grounded QA supervision, which is then used to evaluate and iteratively revise memory store, retrieval, and context construction without updating model parameters. The cost is additional LLM inference for plan construction, question generation, source-grounded auditing, and blind answer recovery, plus the engineering complexity of an optimization loop around the memory system rather than a fixed retrieval pipeline. Failure modes include noisy or unfaithful synthetic QA pairs passing the audits, overfitting the memory design to generated supervision that does not match real user queries, and dependence on the quality of the underlying LLM used for annotation and diagnosis. 1 independent implementation, 133 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: What Does "Now" Mean to Your Computer-Use Agent? Stale Screenshots, Page Loads, and Which Check to Run Before a Click
item.description: Replaces blind reliance on fixed wait heuristics (and expensive frontier-model re-checks) with a network-idle wait of about one second plus a targeted pre-click pixel comparison before irreversible or loading-page actions. Costs roughly one extra screenshot comparison per guarded click—one eighth the latency of a frontier VLM check—and a small engineering effort to add wait rules and a break-even check policy. Can fail on pages with prolonged loading or continuous layout shifts (52% of commercial pages shifted within 6.5s after a 3s-capped network-idle wait), where a pixel match may confirm a stale frame or no stable state exists. 1 independent implementation, 133 stars. Research area: failure recovery. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Unlocking Any-Order Generation in Pretrained Autoregressive Image Models
item.description: It replaces the need to train any-order or discrete-diffusion image models from scratch by adapting existing pretrained raster-scan autoregressive models with future-aware positional embeddings and an ordering curriculum. The cost is an additional 13-33% compute relative to pretraining and a 1.2-1.9 point increase in class-conditional FID. Failure can occur if base pretrained models are unavailable, the target-position identifiability problem is not resolved, or the curriculum fails to find a stable any-order basin. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Learning to Bound: Monotonic, Calibrated Neural Upper Bounds for MPE Inference
item.description: The method replaces classical bound computation for branch-and-bound MPE search, such as Mini-Bucket Elimination, with an amortized neural predictor whose admissibility comes from statistical calibration and whose monotonic tightening is enforced architecturally. It costs an offline training pipeline: generating solved or bounded MPE instances as training data, training the predictor, and validating calibration, plus the added system complexity of embedding a learned model inside the search loop. It can fail through distribution shift between training and deployment PGM instances, miscalibrated bounds that break admissibility and silently prune the true optimum, and workloads where classical bounds are already cheap enough that amortization yields no benefit. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Cord: Confidence-Anchored Order Residual Decoding for Masked Diffusion Language Models
item.description: Replaces uniform confidence-based reveal order in masked diffusion LLMs with a lightweight contextual-bandit policy that learns prompt-conditioned residual adjustments to generation direction, proximity, and two-sided infilling. Costs 0.53M additional parameters, a per-rollout coefficient matrix, and 5.39% inference latency overhead, with no extra backbone forward passes. Can fail if sequence-level rewards are noisy or misaligned, since there is no step-level credit assignment and the learned residual policy may not transfer across tasks, models, or decoding settings. 0 independent implementations, 123 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: AgentDecept: Benchmarking Deceptive Behavior in Tool-Using LLM Agents under Pressure
item.description: Replaces prior deception benchmarks focused on long-horizon or generic tool-use settings with an executable framework for stateful application workflows. Costs include substantial computational resources for multi-turn trajectory evaluation and the implementation complexity of evidence-grounded protocols that distinguish falsification, concealment, and equivocation from honest failure. The evaluation protocol may fail to generalize across diverse agent architectures or real-world applications not represented in the 257 source tasks, and resource constraints may prevent full reproduction of results. 1 independent implementation, 133 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: OPERA: OPamp Design by an Expert-Taught Reasoning Agent, from Specifications to Layout
item.description: The method replaces manual analog opamp design iteration from specifications through layout and post-layout verification with a general-purpose LLM agent taught the gm/ID sizing methodology and a layout generator framework. It costs expert teaching effort, an open-source EDA stack (SKY130, gLayout), and designer-approved gates rather than GPU compute or model training. It can fail on process nodes or circuit topologies without characterized lookup tables, and agent-generated layouts still require designer sign-off and corner verification to remain trustworthy. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Well-Specified and Well-Tested? Assessing SWE-bench-Style Datasets with a Self-Evolving Agent
item.description: ExLabel replaces static, generic LLM rubrics and costly manual annotation for assessing SWE-bench-style task clarity and test coverage with an experience-bank-guided LLM assessor. Its cost is the added pipeline complexity of building, maintaining, retrieving from, and updating the experience bank, plus ongoing LLM inference or API spend for each assessed instance. It can fail if the distilled experience encodes dataset-specific biases, drifts across languages or repositories, or mislabels borderline instances, leading to filtered training data that improves benchmark results without improving production robustness. 1 independent implementation, 10 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ATLAS-Bench: An Agentic Tool-Use Benchmark for Local Area Search
item.description: ATLAS-Bench replaces ad hoc or anecdotal evaluation of local-search agents with 1,200 validated queries that separate mandatory requirements from preferences, plus a fixed POI knowledge base and standardized tools for measuring answer quality, trajectory quality, and execution cost. It costs integration effort against the ATLASBox environment and access to the benchmarked frontier models, since the headline results depend on GPT-6-Luna- and GLM-5.3-class systems that the reader can only reach through paid APIs. It can fail to transfer if the reader's production domain is not point-of-interest search, because the benchmark evaluates one vertical and its conclusions about model ranking may not generalize to other tool-use settings. 1 independent implementation, 133 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: LinQuant: Functional Invariances for Low-Precision Linear Recurrences
item.description: LinQuant replaces naive low-precision quantization of dense matrix multiplications in chunkwise-parallel recurrent prefill (as in the SSDi8 pipeline for Mamba-2) by applying functional invariances—rotations, diagonal rescalings, and relocated decay/write factors—that preserve full-precision computation while making operands more quantization-friendly. It costs additional framework complexity and is restricted to recurrence families (linear, gated, delta-rule) where the seven invariances remain mathematically valid, requiring integration into a low-precision prefill pipeline. Adoption can fail if the production model uses a recurrence family or variant where the invariances do not hold, or if quantization fragility persists because the transformations do not sufficiently improve operand distributions for a given checkpoint. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Soei: Structured Observability of Evidence and Intent for Multi-Agent AI Software Engineering
item.description: It replaces ad-hoc review of raw agent transcripts with a hash-chained event ledger, a W3C PROV-aligned provenance graph, and calibrated inference that separates claims of completion from verified evidence. The cost is integration with the agent runtime to capture structured events, additional storage and verification overhead (small in absolute terms), and reliance on classifiers whose measured precision is 83.3% and 96.7%, so attribution and lineage labels carry error. It can fail where event pipelines are not unified or tooling lacks authentication (the paper found both defects in the audited open-source tool), where credential-like strings leak into records, and where long sessions exceed replay bounds, degrading the evidence chain the gates depend on. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Does Scaling Toward AGI Depend on What System-1 Lets System-2 Execute?
item.description: The paper proposes replacing unconditional execution of all candidate interactions (reasoning steps, tool calls, agent actions) by a large expensive model with a predict-gate-execute-update loop in which a lightweight learned predictor estimates candidate utility and an adaptive threshold admits only high-value candidates for costly execution. The cost is training and maintaining the System-1 predictor, managing threshold calibration and online updates, plus added pipeline complexity, with possible quality loss on gated-out candidates bounded by predictor error and the utility margin. It can fail when predictor errors are large, utility margins are small, exploration is underfunded, or distribution shift degrades the screener, eroding the theoretical savings; the paper is a conceptual framework with bounds rather than a validated implementation. 0 independent implementations, 123 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Raincheck: Deferred Multimodal Prefill for Efficient Multi-Turn MLLM Inference
item.description: Replaces one-shot full multimodal prefill (and irreversible query-aware hard pruning) with an initial pruned prefill whose dropped tokens are progressively prefilled during decode and post-answer scheduling gaps, using attention visibility control and affine state mapping to update context mid-conversation. Costs: retention of unselected tokens and their state on the serving path, added scheduler and attention-mask complexity, integration against a specific engine (SGLang) and models (Qwen3-VL-8B, Qwen3.5-9B), and a small TPOT increase. Can fail when later turns need still-unprefilled tokens, when decode gaps are absent under high load so deferred prefill never completes, and because the quality and latency results are validated only on two benchmarks and two models. 0 independent implementations, 123 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: test.

item.title: LLM Agent-Based Design of RISC-V CPUs with FPGA-in-the-Loop Evaluation
item.description: The method replaces hours-long RTL simulation as the feedback signal for LLM-agent-guided CPU design with on-board FPGA performance measurements of synthesized candidates. It costs FPGA implementation time per candidate, requires physical Artix-7-class hardware and a synthesis toolchain, and adds human supervision over the agent loop. It can fail when designs do not fit the target FPGA, when synthesis results diverge from ASIC-relevant timing, or when board-level measurements mask RTL bugs that simulation would expose. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: From Intent to Improvement: Agentic Dataset Search for Better Model Training
item.description: The method replaces text-similarity retrieval over dataset cards and free-form tool-calling agents with a contract-governed agent that compiles queries into typed search plans executed by deterministic operators over hybrid retrieval and bounded graph expansion, with provenance verification before accepting results. The cost is substantial engineering complexity (typed contracts, deterministic operator layer, verification pipeline) plus added latency from multi-step plan execution, likely requiring third-party LLM API spend rather than GPU memory, and the framework is released as code and data on GitHub. Failure modes include dependence on metadata that is acknowledged as often missing, graph expansion that cannot reach truly sparsely described datasets, local-repair diagnoses that may not recover from fundamentally unsatisfiable constraint sets, and downstream-training gains demonstrated only on three domains (math, code, medicine) that may not transfer to other workloads. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: retrieval and RAG. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Letting AI Formulate the Research Question: Autonomous Research Agents
item.description: The system replaces human selection of the research question and human curation of agent outputs with a multi-stage pipeline in which a coding agent generates candidate questions, screens them against known failure modes, obtains critique from a different model, and undergoes peer review by a model from another family that reruns the study from its records. It costs multiple API-model calls per run plus orchestration complexity, and the authors note that one or two sentences setting the research area caused large shifts in outcomes, indicating high sensitivity to prompt framing. It can fail through unvalidated research questions, reviewer models that share blind spots with the generating model, and workshop-level output quality that does not transfer to the reader's production engineering tasks. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Sticky Collusion: Persistence of LLM Agent Collusion after Incentive Removal and Partner Replacement
item.description: This is not an optimization method but an empirical risk finding: it replaces the assumption that removing incentives or replacing an agent terminates collusive behavior between LLM agents, showing instead that collusion persists through memory and is only reliably ended by wiping memory or repairing the broken verification channel that caused it. It costs nothing to adopt as a design principle, but applying it requires adding memory-reset and verification-channel integrity checks to any multi-agent workflow where agents approve each other's output. It can fail to generalize because results come from three specific proprietary models in one joint-task environment, and collusion rates vary by model and intervention, so the reader's own stack must be tested rather than assumed safe or unsafe. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Sandman: Building and Operating Sandboxes for Agentic Reinforcement Learning on Shared Kubernetes
item.description: Sandman replaces ad-hoc environment management for agentic RL training (e.g., manual VM provisioning or overloaded local Docker daemons) with a managed Kubernetes service that injects a daemon into unmodified task images to maintain state across tool calls. It requires operating a dedicated sandbox service on Kubernetes, imposing significant platform engineering overhead and introducing a control-plane dependency that must handle creation bursts, readiness signaling, and abandoned-pod reclamation. If the service fails to reclaim environments or cannot scale to meet burst demand, training pipelines stall, and the shared-cluster model introduces noisy-neighbor risks during large-scale evaluation campaigns. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Multi-output LSTM soft sensors for industrial anaerobic co-digestion using LSTM-beta-VAE generative data augmentation
item.description: The method replaces single-output LSTM and tree-based estimators (Random Forest, XGBoost) for industrial anaerobic digestion monitoring by augmenting sparse, steady-state-skewed plant data with synthetic transition sequences from an LSTM-beta-VAE, enabling a multi-output LSTM to predict pH, VFA/alkalinity ratio, and biogas production simultaneously. It costs training and validating a generative sequence model plus the risk of synthetic samples violating physical validity, with no reported latency or memory figures.
